deacon `exec` and the reference `exec` present the same TTY allocation to the executed command

an oracle whose reported version differs from the pin is reported as a version mismatch, never silently accepted
an oracle override pointing at a nonexistent binary is reported as a missing oracle, never a skip
a failing Docker probe is reported as docker-missing rather than allowing the check to pass
an oracle that crashes is reported as an oracle failure naming its preserved stderr
non-JSON output where structured output was required is reported as malformed output
an oracle that hangs is terminated at its bound and reported as a timeout with its partial output preserved
an injected difference with no matching waiver is reported as a divergence, never absorbed
a difference matching an active waiver is reported as a waived pass naming the waiver record
a waiver whose characterized difference no longer reproduces is reported as stale rather than silently retained
a normalization failure fails the run; the harness never falls back to raw comparison
a key the reference emits and deacon does not is classified as its own `ref-only` difference class and named
a key deacon emits and the reference does not is reported as its own `deacon-only` difference class and is not ranked below the others as noise
a shared key with differing values is classified as a `value` difference carrying both sides
an accept-versus-reject difference keeps its direction: a waiver characterizing one direction never waives the inverse, and an agreement expectation waives neither
a divergence covered by a scoped tolerance verdicts `allowed-difference` naming its backing record, an uncovered path still verdicts `diverge`, and an unconsumed tolerance is reported stale
a missing snapshot for the current platform verdicts `no-reference-for-platform`, distinct from both `agree` and `stale`, so an absent comparison is never reported as a pass
a snapshot whose evidence-determining provenance drifted is reported stale naming the first drifted field, while a drifted host tool version or capture time is not staleness
`devcontainer.json` mounts are applied by BOTH CLIs on the compose path
deacon's compose project name is isolated from the reference CLI's, so the two CLIs' compose projects never collide
deacon stamps the reference-compatible discovery labels on its container and image while keeping its own isolation labels distinct
a deacon `up` after a reference `up` on the same workspace provisions its own distinct container instead of silently attaching to the reference's
a deacon-generated feature lockfile carries the OCI manifest digest (not the layer digest) and is consumable by the reference CLI's `features resolve-dependencies`
for each CLI independently, `read-configuration --include-merged-configuration` agrees with what `docker inspect` shows on the running container
the primary compose service's rendered image, volumes, environment, and labels compare equal between the two CLIs on equivalent input
deacon and the pinned reference resolve the same configuration document for the basic devcontainer.jsonc fixture
deacon and the pinned reference resolve the same configuration document, including variable substitution, for the with-variables devcontainer.jsonc fixture
each registered corpus discovers at least its declared minimum number of cases
the parity nextest profile selects exactly the registered live binaries and no other profile selects any of them
no parity source uses an ignore attribute or a legacy skip idiom, so a lane can never go green by not running
every registered live and internal-consistency binary has a source file, and every parity source file is registered or a recognized meta-test binary
the tests-directory anchor the registry check walks actually resolves, so a silent no-op scan is impossible
characterized exceptions resolve only from the conformance registry, never from a reintroduced legacy location
`appPort` publishes the same container ports in both CLIs
deacon's compose path folds resolved feature mounts into the container exactly as the reference does
a compose sidecar service and a named volume are provisioned equivalently by both CLIs
the characterized divergence between deacon's and the reference's default workspace-mount target remains exactly as recorded, so a change forces a deliberate decision
a Dockerfile-built workspace with a non-root containerUser/remoteUser yields equivalent container state in both CLIs
deacon's own compose container state matches its single-container state for the same logical configuration, with no reference side involved
read-only bind mounts and tmpfs mounts are applied identically by both CLIs
deacon and the reference produce equivalent inspected container state for a single-container workspace
after `up` on a traditional (non-compose) workspace, both CLIs' `exec` reach that workspace's own container and observe the same environment marker
